title: Harden the fail-closed state-file path: the Stage 1 minor findings on TS-30
description:
Follow-up to the Stage 1 review of opum-ai/test-skills#46 (TS-30). The verdict recorded verbatim on the completed TS-30 record is APPROVE; these are its minor findings that did not block. Filed at the leader's instruction on 2026-10-20. To Do, unclaimed, off the plan.

1. MINOR, gate.py:403-417. The claim that a run reports one violation per bad file is wrong: the try block aborts at the first StateFileError, so with both files corrupt only the first is named and the second surfaces once that is fixed. Still fail-closed. Either say "one per run", or load each file in its own try.

2. MINOR, gate.py:212 vs :215. `ls-tree ... -- path` resolves relative to the cwd (root) while `git show ref:path` resolves from the repo top. With root a subdirectory of the repo and the file present at the base inside that subdirectory, ls-tree says present, show returns empty through the _git swallow, and the gate reports a false unreadable_state_file. It fails closed, not open; the old code had the same mismatch but silently read []. The reverse case cannot happen. Fix with `ref:./path` in show, or `--full-name`. Untested.

5. NIT, test_gate_matrix.py:68,74. Asserting that "quarantine" appears in the message is trivially true because the file name contains it, and the article (XI vs XII) is not asserted, so a mutation that swaps the kind or article labels would survive. Assert the article, and a kind token that is not part of the path.

6. NIT, gate.py:691-696. write_baseline now exits on a corrupt file where it previously swallowed. In the spirit of DEC-213, but it is a behaviour change that nothing tests.

7. NIT, out of scope, noted here so it is not lost: valid JSON of the wrong shape (`{}`, `null`, an entry with no "since") still crashes with a traceback rather than a named violation, at head and at the base.

Findings 3 and 4 from the same review are NOT part of this task.
- Finding 3 is ruled no-change by DEC-213 (a3): "never passes" binds at blocking levels only, so in advisory mode the violation is a named WARN and the passed field stays true.
- Finding 4 is ruled a build by DEC-213 (a2) and gets its own task and PR.

The evidence for every finding is the verbatim verdict on the completed TS-30 record.
